name: Archival matte canvas
why: The default for large pieces. Matte kills glare from downlights and windows, which is what makes canvas readable in a lobby where a glossy print would be a mirror. Stretched over kiln-dried bars that will not warp in humidity.

name: Fine-art paper
why: For work where the surface texture matters — calligraphy, typography, anything with fine linework. Framed behind glazing, so it belongs where hands stay off it.

name: Aluminium composite
spec: 3 mm panel, direct UV print, satin seal
why: Rigid, light and effectively immune to humidity. The right answer for corridors, stairwells and anywhere a canvas would eventually be knocked.

name: Printed wall covering
why: For full-wall and mural work. Fire rating and cleanability are usually the two questions a facilities manager asks first, so the answer is on the spec sheet rather than in a follow-up.
bestFor: Atriums, dining rooms, corridors, feature walls
